metadata.description: Civil resistance tactics catalog - atomic method skills grouped into six domain plugins (governance, economic, labor, communication, social, intervention). Backed by a registry of 347 atomic methods crosswalked from Sharp's 198 Methods and Beer/ICNC Civil Resistance Tactics in the 21st Century. Descriptive for high-risk methods; low-risk methods include preparatory guidance paraphrased from CANVAS, Beautiful Trouble, ICNC, and Swarthmore case studies.

plugins.name: civil-resistance-communication
plugins.description: Communication, symbols, media, and public narrative tactics (domain code comm, registry range 4000-4899). Atomic methods for spoken, written, symbolic, assembly, documentary, and digital expression.

plugins.name: civil-resistance-governance
plugins.description: Governance, political power, legitimacy, elections, and state institution tactics (domain code gov, registry range 1000-1699). Atomic methods for authority challenge, civil disobedience, and pillar-institution noncooperation.

plugins.name: civil-resistance-economic
plugins.description: Economic pressure, boycott, divestment, and alternative-economy tactics (domain code econ, registry range 2000-2899). Atomic methods for consumer, supplier, financial, trade, and property action.

plugins.name: civil-resistance-labor
plugins.description: Labor, workplace, strike, and professional noncooperation tactics (domain code labr, registry range 3000-3799). Atomic methods for symbolic, sectoral, restricted, and constructive labor action.

plugins.name: civil-resistance-social
plugins.description: Social, community, cultural, and religious relations tactics (domain code soc, registry range 5000-5899). Atomic methods for ostracism, withdrawal, parallel institutions, and identity-based solidarity.

plugins.name: civil-resistance-intervention
plugins.description: Nonviolent intervention, presence, obstruction, and parallel-institution tactics (domain code intv, registry range 6000-6899). Atomic methods for physical presence, self-exposure, protective accompaniment, and service intervention.
